title: Previous-month NAO gave no clear added Scotland winter rain information after current NAO in 1981-2025
abstract: We tested whether previous-month North Atlantic Oscillation (NAO) adds information about Scotland winter monthly rain after current-month NAO is known. Models used earlier winters from 1951 onward and 135 test months in 1981-2025. Adding lag NAO after current NAO gave a -0.42% MSE reduction. The conditional 95% five-winter score-block interval was -3.10% to +2.15%. Without current NAO, the matching lag gain was 7.76%. Raw rain, trend and rain-lag checks gave no clear conditional gain. Lag NAO also reduced current-NAO prediction MSE by 13.79%, with limits of 1.17% to 23.49%. The results are consistent with circulation persistence as one explanation for a prior campaign rain forecast result. They do not prove a cause or a zero remaining lag effect. Current NAO makes the main comparison a reconstruction, not a forecast. Shared revised data, one country, linear models, prior result selection and conditional uncertainty limit inference. Code, aggregate results, source hashes, external retrieval instructions, a figure and numerical checks are included. External raw data and monthly derived records remain outside the bundle.

display.caption: Previous-month NAO gain without and with current-month NAO. Points show test MSE reduction; bars show conditional 95% five-winter block limits. Current NAO uses information from the target month.
